stories.title: OpenCode Hacked: User credentials leaked
stories.reason: Confirmed breach: OpenCode's console disclosed unauthorized access to a legacy system exposing stored OpenAI/Anthropic/Google API keys for 1.4% of console users; CLI-only users unaffected. Concrete, high-impact AI-tooling security incident, 775 HN points.
key_facts: OpenCode disclosed on X/email Oct 17-18 2026
Described as a 'large scale distillation attack' impacting 1.4% of OpenCode Console users
Exposed third-party provider keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, possibly Google) saved in users' workspaces
CLI-only users with local-env keys were not affected
At least one user reported ~$400 in unauthorized Anthropic charges before catching it
OpenCode working with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google on remediation; incident ongoing

stories.title: Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude
stories.reason: Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 autonomously redesigned 8 quantum circuits in a closed evaluator loop, beating published records (e.g. 17x fewer gates on elliptic-curve point addition, ~12x gate reduction on a Reed-Solomon decoder vs Google's construction) — a concrete, verifiable AI-for-science result with numbers, not a demo.
key_facts: Claude given 8 plain-language quantum-circuit specs (chemistry, optimization, physics sim, number theory)
Worked in closed loop with automated evaluator, no human input between rounds; score = qubits x gates
Elliptic-curve point addition: 53 hours of work, 12% more qubits but 17x fewer gates than smallest prior design

Reed-Solomon decoder: switched to Berlekamp-Massey decoding, cut gate count ~12x vs Google's prior construction; worst-case storage fell from 665 qubits to a 19-qubit reserve (403M simulated decodings, ~1-in-10,000 failure rate)
Model was overly cautious/conservative; team had to force parallel divergent approaches
No code repo linked; only the arXiv paper (2610.22367)

stories.title: Why harnesses matter for energy (and token) efficiency
stories.reason: Data-driven look (30 days production traffic + controlled lab tests) at how agent harnesses affect prompt-cache hit rate, and therefore energy/latency: cache misses cost 91-140% more energy per request, and client choice swings uncached-input rate from 1.6% to 11.1%. Directly on the 'how models are served' line the profile cares about.
key_facts: Uncached-input share by client: 1.6% (deepseek-harness) to 11.1% (Node.js apps); 92% cached implies ~2.7x the prefill work of 97% cached
Cache-break rate ~1/100 turns for deepseek-harness vs ~3/100 for OpenCode and Pi
A mostly-uncached request used ~91% more energy on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, ~140% more on GLM-5.3
Past 128k tokens, ~3/1000 turns re-read most of the prompt; one such turn costs as much prefill as ~600 normal turns (TTFT 5-41s vs 0.8-2.8s)
Lab test: 65 of 539 follow-up requests across 4 agents broke the cache, e.g. via OpenCode's plan-mode reminder
Caveat: published by Neuralwatt, which sells the cloud service being measured

stories.title: Apple ML Research: Muse Spark Open with MLX on Mac Studio
stories.reason: Apple ML Research shows distributed MLX inference across multiple Mac Studios (new jaccl RDMA-over-Thunderbolt backend) running Muse Spark Open (816B MoE, NVFP4) at ~37 tok/s on 4x M5 Ultra, with full runnable commands — concrete serving-efficiency numbers and working code, not just a benchmark claim.
key_facts: 4x M5 Ultra tensor-parallel: 36.73 tok/s on Muse Spark Open (816B MoE, NVFP4) at 8K context
2x M5 Ultra: 24.99 tok/s (tensor) vs 15.74 tok/s (pipeline)
New 'jaccl' communication backend (MLX 0.30.1+) built on macOS 26.2's low-latency RDMA-over-Thunderbolt driver, needed for tensor parallelism to pay off
Single M5 Ultra vs M3 Ultra: up to 4.6x faster time-to-first-token, ~1.6x faster decode (1.2TB/s vs 819GB/s memory bandwidth)
Peak power ~300W (M5 Ultra) vs ~200W (M3 Ultra)
Runnable via mlx.launch / mlx_lm.benchmark / mlx_lm.server; links MLX LM GitHub repo

stories.title: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017
stories.reason: DeepSeek ships V4.1-Flash-1017, a 763B-param MIT-licensed open-weight update with concrete benchmark deltas over prior Flash (HLE, Terminal-Bench, DeepSWE). High HN visibility (701/511 pts across two postings) means saturation is already high, but still the clearest open-weight release of the day.
key_facts: 763B parameters, MIT license, 1M token context
HLE (no tools) 42.6 vs 36.8 for prior Flash
Terminal-Bench 4.0: 42.3 vs 31.2; DeepSWE v1.1: 77.0 vs 74.2; ProgramBench 29.1 vs 20.3
Compared against K3, GLM-5.3, GPT-5.6 Sol, Opus 5 — leads on DeepSWE, trails Opus 5 on most other rows
No Jinja chat template; ships a Python reference impl plus a Rust 'deepseek-recipe' library
Framed by DeepSeek itself as a minor update, not a new flagship generation

stories.title: Llama.cpp on a jailbroken PS5: run any GGUF model natively on the console
stories.reason: PS5LM runs GGUF models via llama.cpp's Vulkan backend on a jailbroken PS5's GPU, serving OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoints to the whole LAN — real running code (~513 stars, public releases) with concrete per-model throughput, squarely in the 'running code beats a description' lane.
key_facts: GPL-3.0, llama.cpp Vulkan backend, ~11.4GB shared memory on PS5 GPU (RDNA2)
Serves OpenAI /v1/chat/completions and Anthropic /v1/messages on port 8081, plus browser chat UI
Qwen 3.5 0.8B Q4_K_M: 207 tok/s; Qwen 3.5 9B Q4_K_M: 55 tok/s; Qwen 3.8 27B UD-Q2_K_XL: ~20 tok/s at 64k ctx
Requires jailbroken PS5 firmware 7.00-13.60 plus several homebrew payloads (kstuff-lite, etaHEN, etc.)
~513 GitHub stars, public app release, 11 open issues

stories.title: Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak
stories.reason: Sophos reports (via OpenAI's own customer-story post) cutting MDR threat-investigation time 96% and resolving 52% of cases end-to-end with AI agents built on OpenAI Daybreak. Concrete vendor-reported numbers on AI x cyber/SOC automation, though self-reported and unverified by a third party.
key_facts: OpenAI customer story published Oct 9, 2026
Claimed: 96% reduction in threat-investigation time, 89s average AI-agent response time, 52% of MDR cases resolved end-to-end by AI agents
Secondary coverage cites a pre-Daybreak baseline of ~38 min/case (not confirmed in OpenAI's own text)
Vendor-reported figures; no independent verification found

stories.title: Amazon uses AI to monitor union risk in UK warehouses
stories.reason: Leaked internal docs describe Amazon's 'Atlas' system scoring warehouses on unionization risk using hundreds of signals (including scraping worker Reddit/forum activity), with two UK sites (Coventry, Minworth) flagged Tier 1 — a concrete, documented case of AI used for labor surveillance, not a vague trend piece.
key_facts: Documents surfaced via a Canadian labour dispute (Unifor certification at Amazon's YVR2 warehouse, BC Labour Relations Board)
Atlas inputs reportedly include worker comms channels, safety incidents, minimum wage, proximity to unionized warehouses
Also monitors external forums like Reddit, tracking phrases/keywords and upvote patterns
UK sites Coventry and Minworth (active GMB organizing) rated 'Tier 1' risk
Separate Fairwork/GPAI interview-based study also found AI/robotics in UK Amazon warehouses isolates workers and hampers organizing
